0.long_answer: Vitreous humor analysis in masquerade syndrome, particularly when differentiating primary vitreoretinal lymphoma (PVRL) from inflammatory uveitis, involves testing for a specific mutation. The mutation identified is the MYD88 L265P mutation. This mutation is present in approximately 80-90% of cases, making it a highly specific marker for PVRL. Its detection via PCR-based methods in the vitreous humor helps confirm the diagnosis, especially when other diseases have been ruled out.
